name: Major cyber incidents
summary: A cyberattack on Guadeloupe's university hospital from 22 Nov forced paper records and postponed planned care
state: Guadeloupe's university hospital triggered its emergency plan on 22 Nov after a cyberattack disabled IT systems and phone lines across its sites; planned operations were postponed and emergency calls still work (Outre-mer La 1ère). CISA added nine exploited flaws to its catalogue in the week to 23 Nov, including VMware vCenter, SAP and Cisco flaws on 20 Nov (CISA). Disruption to a hospital keeps Watch; no national-scale attack was found.
for_you: Patients of affected hospitals should follow the hospital's and local health authority's instructions; in France, call 15 in an emergency. Organisations can check CISA's exploited-vulnerabilities catalogue and NCSC guidance for patching.
rubric_hit: Attack disrupting a critical service (hospital) = Watch; no national-scale attack

sources.title: Outre-mer La 1ère — Cyberattaque au CHU de Guadeloupe, plan blanc déclenché

why: Ransomware and state hacking now shut down hospitals, retailers, carmakers and airports for weeks.
drivers: Ransomware gangs, state actors, zero-days, supply-chain compromises.

rubric.alert: National-scale attack on critical infrastructure (power, health, finance), or a destructive state-attributed attack.
rubric.watch: Ransomware or attack disrupting a large company or critical service, or a mass-exploited zero-day.
rubric.normal: No major incidents disrupting critical services this week.
